title: Smooth comparison for two embedded-compatible ordinary towers
statement: Fix L and a synchronized embedded resolution assignment E [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution]. Let S,T be embeddable reduced finite-type rational inputs, A and B intrinsic labeled ordinary towers on them, and a,b identifications of A,B with E for every permitted embedding [def-trf-intrinsic-labeled-resolution]. For every smooth rational morphism h:T to S there exists a contracted cartesian comparison c of B with A: its center ideals are the extended ideals, and it retains exactly the nonunit labels. For every pair of permitted embeddings p,q and cartesian smooth ambient map f:q to p whose intrinsic map is h under their initial isomorphisms, c.map followed by a(p) equals b(q) followed by E.pullback(f).intrinsic. This is a statement about two fixed towers, not an existence theorem for an intrinsic assignment.

source.place: VIII 2.1.1--2.1.9, 2.3.1, 2.3.4--2.3.5, 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.86--88,91--94. Agent expansion of the conditional embedded-to-intrinsic argument, not a separately quoted ILO theorem.

proof.text: Fix embeddings p of S and q of T and use a(p), b(q) to compare their embedded diagrams with the given A and B. For an open U of either input X inside its ambient P, take the ambient open O=P minus (X minus U). Its inclusion is etale, hence smooth. The closed square U=X times_P O is cartesian. The ambient P is Noetherian because it is finite type over Q; O is therefore quasi-compact and locally of finite type, hence finite type. Smoothness and separatedness restrict to O. Thus E.pullback provides a cartesian open comparison. Convert any auxiliary chart embedded towers to ordinary towers by [lem-trf-embedded-resolution-ordinary-tower]. Rigidity makes comparisons on open overlaps independent of ambient opens and of the embeddings.

Cover the smooth h by standard-smooth affine charts V -> U. Since the inputs are finite type over Q, the affine coordinate ring of U is finitely generated over Q. Choose a presentation R/I with R a finite polynomial Q-algebra, so U embeds in Spec R. The polynomial algebra is standard smooth with no equations, and its spectrum is a smooth separated finite-type ambient. These choices are only local auxiliary data; they do not change the fixed towers A and B.

Lift the standard-smooth algebra C of V across R -> R/I by the standard-smooth quotient lifting theorem. It gives a standard-smooth R-algebra D with D/ID isomorphic to C. Thus Q=Spec D is smooth over Spec R, finite type and affine, hence separated, and smooth over Q by composition. The square V=U times_(Spec R) Q is cartesian. Apply E.pullback on this square, then the supplied intrinsic identifications and the open comparisons of the first step. This gives chartwise comparisons for the restrictions of the fixed A and B, preserving every actual ideal, not merely its support.

Index the two fixed towers by the union of their finite active label sets. At the first cut the comparison is h under the initial isomorphisms. Suppose the comparison has been constructed through a cut. The inverse images of the V chart opens cover this current source level. The open and embedded chart comparisons identify its proposed center ideal with the extended center ideal on the target. The preceding chart maps agree with the induction maps by rigidity, so these are equalities of ideals on the same scheme. Ideal-sheaf equality is local, hence the ideals agree globally. Unit ideals can likewise be tested on the cover, proving that no new label appears and precisely the unit stages disappear.

Each projection at the current cut is a smooth base change of h, hence flat. Flat blowup base change produces the next cartesian square from the equality of center ideals. If the extended ideal is unit its Rees algebra is O[t], whose Proj is the current scheme, so that step is an identity. The finite induction provides the map of cut diagrams, naturality, all cartesian squares, the centers equality and the retained-label equivalence.

On each chart the constructed comparison and the embedded comparison are the lifts of the same preceding maps with the same ideals; rigidity identifies them. The same applies to any supplied cartesian smooth ambient square f between any permitted p and q, after conjugating by a(p), b(q). It gives c.map followed by a(p) equal to b(q) followed by E.pullback(f).intrinsic, exactly the claimed compatibility. This also proves independence of all chart and lift choices. The construction uses only affine neighbourhoods, so it imposes neither separation nor constant relative dimension on h. Empty towers, non-surjective h and charts missing centers are covered by the unit-ideal case.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_intrinsic_smooth_comparison
    {L : Type w} [LinearOrder L] (E : SynchronizedEmbeddedResolution.{u, w} L)
    (S T : EmbeddableResolutionInput.{u})
    (A : IntrinsicLabeledOrdinaryTower L S.val.scheme)
    (B : IntrinsicLabeledOrdinaryTower L T.val.scheme)
    (a : ∀ p : RationalResolutionEmbedding S.val,
      IntrinsicEmbeddedResolutionIdentification A p (E.tower p.pair))
    (b : ∀ q : RationalResolutionEmbedding T.val,
      IntrinsicEmbeddedResolutionIdentification B q (E.tower q.pair))
    (h : T.val.scheme ⟶ S.val.scheme)
    (_over : h ≫ S.val.structureMap = T.val.structureMap) [Smooth h] :
    ∃ c : IntrinsicLabeledResolutionPullback h A B,
      ∀ (p : RationalResolutionEmbedding S.val) (q : RationalResolutionEmbedding T.val)
        (f : EmbeddedResolutionSmoothMap q.pair p.pair),
        q.iso.hom ≫ f.intrinsic = h ≫ p.iso.hom →
          c.map ≫ (a p).iso.hom = (b q).iso.hom ≫ (E.pullback f).intrinsic
